newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slow in pre-holiday trade - dealers. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slow in pre-holiday trade - dealers. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased in early trade on Wednesday as the market wound down ahead of the independence day holiday on Thursday.
They saw the market little changed overall despite expectations individual stocks could see significant activity.
The opening figure for the Russian Trading System 22-share index was unavailable for technical reasons. The index closed slightly down on Tuesday at 365.26.

"The mood is pre-holiday -- people are actively preparing for a break," said Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Yevgeny Skibitsky. "It's quiet for now. There are some offers, but prices are going down a little."
National power company UES slipped to $0.3145 from $0.3150 at 0900 GMT, while oil company LUKoil, which has made strong gains in past days, eased to $15.54 from $15.60.
Traders said interest remained strong in undervalued second-tier stocks, especially in regional telecoms, power companies and defence enterprises.

Traders said telecom Kursk Elektrosvyaz was among the strongest shares, with offers at $7.40 and bids at $6 after closing on Tuesday at $7. Power company Rostovenergo was trading at around $0.1370 after closing at $0.1390.
Traders said leading shares by contrast were quiet, continuing a trend of the past few days, but said the market remained healthy overall.

"There are still healthy flows in blue chips," said Peter Halloran, chief of equities at CS First Boston, adding he did not think recent rapid growth on the second tier was at the expense of leading shares.
He said a new spurt of growth in the market overall would come when investors revised their valuations of Russian equity upwards after recent falls in government security yields.
"The dramatic improvement in the fixed income market is more what people should be focused on -- that's where the next leg up comes, from that awareness," Halloran said.
But traders did not see major market movements in the short term.

"The holidays will make speculators restructure their books," Skibitsky said. "It's possible there will be strong movement in different directions on individual stocks, but overall the market will see insignificant fluctuations."
